description: Prometheus and Loki responses reshaped into the field-based graph contract with ordinary dashboard transformations. Every fixture reproduces a real datasource frame shape: predictable_csv_wave is a metric query (one frame per series, value field named Value), csv_content is an instant query with Format: Table. One joinByField on Time does the widening; filter.byRefId separates two queries in one panel. The PromQL/LogQL is in every panel description.

options.content:
# Prometheus and Loki data

Prometheus and Loki range queries usually return one frame for each series. Join by field on `Time` combines those frames into one wide frame.

Set the legend to `source-->target` so each edge field contains both endpoint names. If the query provides `source` and `target` labels, the panel can read the endpoints from those labels.

If a panel has separate edge and node queries, filter each join by query letter. This keeps the two frame types separate.

### Prometheus panels

The service Graph joins one edge query and one node error-ratio query. Each query uses a separate transformation filtered by query letter.

The CPU Sankey combines node-to-namespace and namespace-to-workload edges.

The cross-zone Chord keeps cycles and self-links. Use Chord for a traffic matrix that contains both directions.

The instant-table Graph creates edge ids with `label_join`. Organize fields and Rows to fields convert its rows into fields.

panels.title: Service dependency map — graph
panels.description: Prometheus query A provides service-call edges. Query B provides the error ratio for each server node. Separate Join by field transformations keep edges and nodes in different frames. Graph keeps the cycle in the service calls.

panels.title: Kubernetes CPU requests — sankey
panels.description: Two Prometheus queries provide node-to-namespace and namespace-to-workload edges. Join by field gives each edge a field name. The input has no node frame, so the panel derives nodes from the endpoints.

panels.title: Cross-AZ request matrix — chord
panels.description: A Prometheus query groups Istio requests by source and destination zone. Chord keeps both directions and self-links. Ribbon width shows the request rate.

panels.title: The table route — graph, instant + label_join
panels.description: This Prometheus instant-table query creates an edge `id` with `label_join`. Organize fields and Rows to fields convert each row into an edge field. The `source` and `target` labels provide the endpoints.

options.content:
### Loki panels

LogQL metric queries return the same multi-frame shape as Prometheus range queries. Join by field on `Time` uses the legend names as edge field names.

The service Graph shows calls between services from structured logs. The log-volume Sankey combines cluster-to-namespace and namespace-to-level flows.

The page-transition Chord keeps forward links, back links, and self-links. The parallel-edge Graph groups by `protocol`, so HTTP and gRPC can connect the same nodes.

panels.title: Service call graph from structured logs — graph
panels.description: A LogQL metric query counts calls between services. Join by field converts the series into edge fields. Sum shows the total count over the selected time range.

panels.title: Log volume by cluster → namespace → level — sankey
panels.description: Two LogQL queries provide cluster-to-namespace and namespace-to-level edges. Ribbon width shows the log count. The input has no node frame, so the panel derives nodes from the endpoints.

panels.title: Page-transition matrix from ingress access logs — chord
panels.description: A LogQL metric query groups ingress logs by referrer path and destination path. Chord keeps forward links, back links, and the `/home` self-link.

panels.title: Parallel edges via label_format — graph
panels.description: The LogQL query creates `source` and `target` labels from JSON fields and groups by `protocol`. HTTP and gRPC therefore appear as separate edges between the same nodes.

panels.title: PR rollout by wave — the frame, and whether it suits this family

options.content:
### Rollout examples

The rollout query returns one row for each deployment wave. Rows to fields converts the rows into node fields. Field labels keep the version and estimated completion time.

The Graph uses a second query for edges between consecutive waves. Fixed positions show the rollout from left to right. A threshold colors each wave by `is_in_build`.

The Sankey connects each wave to its current version. Ribbon width shows how many waves use each version. Derived version nodes have no measured value.

panels.title: PR rollout by wave — graph
panels.description: Each deployment wave is a node. Fixed positions show the rollout from left to right. A threshold on `is_in_build` colors each wave. Select a node to see its version and estimated completion time.
